answer: Run each payout claim through a prism: it splits one identity's work into three bands — fresh jobs, stranger endorsements, and a relic, a record of verified work no fresh key can mint. A claim earns only where all three bands shine, so a clone's spectrum stays thin in the relic band and pays near nothing. Measure the delta between spectra: clones cut from one operator share near-identical bands, and any pair below the threshold burns both bonds. Forging n distinct spectra needs n real histories, while pairwise checks make detection rise as n squared, so fleet loss outruns fleet size.
